height_note: 0.83 from the survey; ds package page not re-read
kicad_symbol_check: LSM6DSL symbol has the same numbering as ds p11 table 2 (1 SDO/SA0, 2 SDx, 3 SCx, 4 INT1, 5 VDDIO, 6 GND, 7 GND, 8 VDD, 9 INT2, 12 CS, 13 SCL, 14 SDA). Its pins 10/11 are NC: on the LSM6DSV16X they are OCS_Aux/SDO_Aux, to be left unconnected in mode 1 (p47 note 1). No LSM6DSV16X symbol exists.

circuit.role: Qvar electrode series resistors (figure 29 shows 500 ohm; rest of the network not transcribed)

logic: levels follow Vdd_IO. INT1/INT2 are push-pull at Vdd_IO by default; open-drain and active-low are register options.

i2c_addr.bus: I2C_S (1.8 V segment recommended, see notes)

placement: Near the middle of the board, away from the keyboard dome area and the slider rails (shock), firmly supported; axes square to the board edges.
Qvar (electrostatic field): pins 2 and 3 go to two small copper electrode pads on an outer surface/edge of the case, as far apart as practical; works in I2C mode 1 only (p34).
notes: CONFLICT with the pin plan: IMU_INT_N is a 1.8 V wake pad and INT1 is a push-pull output at Vdd_IO. Recommended: run the IMU (Vdd and Vdd_IO) from 1.8 V and put it on the 1.8 V bus segment with the AS7341, so INT1 can never exceed 1.8 V; firmware then sets open-drain, active-low. This needs a 1.8 V rail that stays up in the sleep state motion should wake from. Fallback: 3.3 V supply, INT1 through a series Schottky diode (cathode to INT1) so it can only pull the pad low.
0x6A is also the BQ25895's address, but that one is on I2C_P: no clash.
